title: Birgitta Böckeler - State of Play: AI Coding Assistants - AI Native DevCon June 2026
summary: Thoughtworks' Birgitta Böckeler gives a balanced state-of-play on models, harnesses and context engineering, arguing for deterministic sensors and risk-based supervision while flagging rising costs in stability, review load, cognitive load and skills.

assertions.quote: it comes with the trade off on like how well the models are able to keep attention on all of the many instructions

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: reflection on the types of tasks that we have and then match them to different levels of power that the the models have

verdicts.note: Model strengths do differ by task in benchmarks and practice, but the specific pairing is personal preference and shifts each release.

assertions.quote: even that model was still struggling a bit with tool calling, which is really crucial for our workflows

verdicts.note: Qwen3-Coder, Kimi K2 and GLM 4.5/4.6 posted strong SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench results in 2025 while generally trailing frontier closed models.

assertions.quote: so that we can trigger immediately a self-correction loop before we even look at the code

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: anytime you find an agent makes a mistake, you take the time to engineer a solution such that the agent never makes that mistake again

verdicts.note: Encoding lessons in rules and workflows does reduce repeat mistakes, but rule files bloat and conflict if not pruned; gains are real but not automatically compounding.

assertions.quote: It's much more effective to have this linting rule than to like stuff it into your context every single time the agent runs.

verdicts.note: Deterministic checks fire every time and give agents concrete feedback, whereas instruction-file rules compete for attention and are followed inconsistently.

assertions.quote: code mods being made available to AI. So that combination is really powerful

verdicts.note: Migration case studies (Google, Amazon Java upgrades, Airbnb) got their scale from pairing LLMs with deterministic tooling and validation rather than free-form generation.

assertions.quote: in the Dora report this was one of the big like let's say negative trend findings about stability actually getting worse

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 reports AI adoption now positively associated with throughput while still associated with higher delivery instability (change failure and rework).

assertions.quote: We have higher coding throughput. But then can we if we can code faster, can we review faster

verdicts.note: Surveys and studies (e.g. Faros, Google) report increased PR volume and review load with AI adoption.

assertions.quote: It doesn't actually make us make our lives more relaxed. On the contrary.

verdicts.note: Many practitioner reports and some surveys describe higher intensity and fatigue from supervising agents, but controlled evidence is thin and other studies report reduced effort on routine work.

assertions.quote: AI can also deal with a well factored code base much better than with a messy code base

verdicts.note: Clear module boundaries help both humans and agents navigate and test; consistent with Ousterhout and practitioner reports.

assertions.quote: Or I can't work on this code base without AI anymore, right? That's the original cognitive surrender cognitive debt kind of definition.

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.
